Link to Vote: https://dao.ckb.community/thread/vot-vellum-reputation-extension-on-did-ckb-77380

Context

This is a resubmission. The first proposal (discussion thread) did not pass the voting stage. The main opposition, once clarified in the thread post-vote, rested on a factual misunderstanding about ckb:did rather than a scoped concern with Vellum. @ckb-ccc/did-ckb is live and the underlying stack is real, active, and usable today.

The proposal is largely unchanged in scope. Refinements in this revision:

  • Payment structure aligned with the community’s preferred 25% / 25% / 25% / 25% split.
  • Framing clarified to make Vellum’s independence from the upstream proposer’s roadmap explicit.

Everything else, including the $7,000 total, testnet-only scope, and CKBoost integration, is the same as before.

Summary

One-Paragraph Overview

This proposal requests a grant of $7,000 to strengthen Vellum, the reference dashboard and SDK for did:ckb, and extend it from identity into reputation, building and rigorously testing the work on testnet with a real integration into CKBoost.

Deliverables:

  • Open, on-chain claim Cell format and SDK additions to @ckb-ccc/did-ckb.
  • Scoring engine that issues verified social signals against a builder’s DID.
  • Public builder reputation dashboard with per-category score breakdown.
  • CKBoost integration where quest-completion points feed reputation scoring.
  • Governance gating reference plus a mini interactive demo that consumes the primitive to resist Sybil-style manipulation of voting.
  • Issuance UI for future ecosystem partners (builders who are actively working on POAP, crowdfunding, and gated sub-communities).
  • Vellum webpage improvements and acquisition of its own domain.

All deliverables ship on testnet.

Grant Amount Requested: $7,000 USD equivalent, paid in CKB at the USD value at the time of each disbursement

ETA to Completion: 12 weeks from disbursement of initial funding

CKB Wallet or Funding Address: ckb1qyqvhfqtwyjhgeha6qnmcxp4veljkn5ty64qzt7v3l

Project Introduction

What problem are we solving. Reputation is the natural extension of the did:ckb identity primitive and a necessary foundation for a wide range of applications, especially governance. CKB’s emerging governance designs need a Sybil-resistant signal to gate eligibility or weight participation, and there is no portable on-chain reputation primitive for them to consult today. The gap is also concrete at the platform layer: CKBoost runs the task and quest infrastructure builders interact with today but has an under-developed identity stack of its own, and the quest-completion points it tracks live in its own database with no portable representation. Builder activity is scattered across CKBoost, hackathons, bounties, and event organizer notes, and none of it is queryable by a governance contract that wants to check whether a participant has genuinely contributed before granting them weight. The result is that any governance program trying to weight by participation has to either build its own private reputation pipeline or fall back to pure token weighting, which is the manipulation surface the whole design is trying to avoid.

What this addresses. The Vellum reputation extension attaches a queryable, portable record of ecosystem participation to a builder’s did:ckb. CKBoost is the immediate plugin integration target: its quest-completion points become signed claim Cells against the participating builder’s DID, giving CKBoost a richer identity layer and giving Vellum a real source of legitimate participation signals to score against. Verified social handles, on-chain history, event attendance (issued by platforms like CKB-PoP), and peer recognitions become additional claim Cells signed by their respective issuers and locked to the holder’s DID. Any CKB app can read the full record with one SDK call. Governance is the load-bearing long-term consumer: upcoming CKBuilders programs around POAP-style eligibility, crowdfunding, and gated sub-communities (all tracked at Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects) can consume the record to gate access, weight participation, or distribute funds based on demonstrated contribution rather than token balance alone. Other platforms that already track participation (CKB-PoP, future grant DAOs) can become issuers without changing their core products.

Why now

Three things just lined up:

  • The basic did:ckb infrastructure is shipping. Vellum v1 is live on testnet and mainnet (claim, edit, rotate, deactivate, resolve, did:plc migrate). The advanced SDK PR (@ckb-ccc/did-ckb, PR #376) has been merged into CCC and is live in the published @ckb-ccc/did-ckb package on npm. The DID stack is at the point where it needs real integration testing to mature, and a reputation extension is the natural next layer.
  • CKBoost runs the task and quest infrastructure builders interact with today but has an under-developed identity stack of its own. CKBoost is also on testnet, where Vellum can iterate safely against it. Integrating Vellum as a plugin enhances CKBoost’s identity layer while giving Vellum a real source of participation signals to score against.
  • Governance designs are actively being explored in the ecosystem, including upcoming CKBuilders programs that focus on POAP-style eligibility, crowdfunding, and gated sub-communities. These all need a manipulation-resistant input that is not another token balance, and none exists today. Reputation is a prerequisite for any governance design that wants to weight by participation rather than token holdings, and the audit-before-implementation bar makes a testnet-first reputation primitive the responsible path.

Team & Roles

  • Name / Handle: @truthixify
  • Role: Solo developer covering smart contracts, SDK, frontend, and design.
  • Experience / Relevant background: Built Vellum v1 from spec to mainnet. Upstreamed the advanced did:ckb operations to @ckb-ccc/did-ckb (PR #376, reviewed and merged into CCC). Previously built Haven, a social identity prototype with a privacy / ZK layer. The transparency-first reputation design in this proposal is informed by what worked and what did not in that prior attempt: stamps and signals are public; privacy is provided through the holder’s right to destroy any record.
  • Why CKB: The Cell model is uniquely suited to this work. Subject-owned claim Cells with capacity-recovery on destruction give holders sovereignty that EVM-based attestation systems cannot match cleanly. Capacity-as-storage-rent makes the economics of issuer-pays attestations natural rather than a tax. Type-id-derived identifiers give did:ckb self-authenticating IDs as a chain primitive, matching the property did:plc achieves via SHA-256-of-genesis-op but with the directory replaced by the chain itself.

Links:

  • GitHub: truthixify · GitHub
  • Vellum repository: GitHub - truthixify/vellum: Dashboard for managing did:ckb identities. Your identity, on paper that lasts. · GitHub
  • Haven repository (prior work): GitHub - truthixify/haven · GitHub

Current Status

  • Vellum v1: live on testnet and mainnet. Full identity surface is shipping: claim, edit, rotate, deactivate, resolve, and did:plc migration. The services.profile convention (displayName, avatar, bio inline under a service entry) implemented in both the dashboard and the SDK.
  • SDK upstreamed and shipped. Advanced operations PR feat(did-ckb): identifier helpers, resolver, history walk, did:plc migration by truthixify · Pull Request #376 · ckb-devrel/ccc · GitHub to ckb-devrel/ccc was reviewed and merged into CCC. The PR adds resolver, history walk, did:plc migration via WIP-02 witness, and full transaction builders, on top of the basic DID operations the CCC team already shipped. Live in the published @ckb-ccc/did-ckb package on npm.
  • Forum context. Original Vellum thread: Vellum: a reference dashboard and SDK for did:ckb. Reputation extension follow-up where this work is laid out in detail: Vellum, extended: from identity to reputation on did:ckb.
  • Live URL: https://vellum-lyart.vercel.app/

Application Design

This section explains how the system actually functions.

6.1 Functional Overview

A builder’s flow through the system:

  1. Claim a did:ckb. Through Vellum’s existing identity flow, the user mints a did:ckb Cell on testnet.
  2. Link social accounts. GitHub, Discord, Telegram, Bluesky. Each link is verified via an OAuth proof or a post-with-DID proof, then written as a signed claim Cell against the builder’s DID.
  3. Accumulate recognitions. Platforms that already track participation (CKBoost via successful quests, CKB-PoP via event attendance, future grant DAOs via grant completions) sign claim Cells attesting to what they observed. Each claim is a small on-chain record signed by the issuer’s key.
  4. Be queried. Any CKB app calls readClaims(client, { subject: did }) and gets back the full structured record. Governance programs (gated sub-communities, POAP-style eligibility checks, grant programs) consume it to gate access or weight participation against demonstrated activity rather than token holdings alone. Wallets render verified socials. Grant programs check it for Sybil resistance.
  5. Stay in control. Every claim Cell is locked to the subject. The holder can destroy any Cell they do not want public, recovering the capacity. No claim is unrevocable from the holder’s side.

On-chain vs off-chain: the DID and the claim Cells are on chain. Social-platform OAuth verification, scoring computation, and dashboard rendering are off chain. There is no Vellum database for reputation data; all data lives in Cells.

6.2 Architecture & Design

New on-chain components:

  • Claim Cell Type Script. Validates the shape of a claim (issuer DID, subject DID, schema string, DAG-CBOR payload, issuer signature). Subject’s lock script controls destruction.

New off-chain components:

  • Scoring engine. Stateless service that pulls signals from connected social platforms via OAuth and writes signed claim Cells. No database.
  • Public builder profile page (the reputation dashboard). New Vellum surface at /profile/<did> that renders identity, verified socials, on-chain history, issued recognitions, and a reputation score with a per-category breakdown (technical, community, contribution, tenure, recency, etc.) derived from the claim history for any DID.
  • Governance gating reference implementation. A small reference contract (or off-chain checker, depending on the consuming program’s design) that reads readClaims to determine eligibility, derive participation weight from claim history, or both. Ships with documented integration patterns so other governance programs (gated sub-communities, POAP-style eligibility checks, grant programs) can adapt it. Testnet only in this proposal, pending audit.
  • CKBoost plugin integration (testnet). A working bidirectional integration with CKBoost: Vellum DID becomes the identity layer CKBoost can plug into, and CKBoost-signed quest-completion claims feed the Vellum scoring engine. Co-designed with @Alive24 against CKBoost’s existing testnet deployment.
  • Issuance UI for ecosystem partners. A simple form-based interface for issuers (CKB-PoP organizers, future grant DAOs, anyone with a credible attestation to make) to issue a claim without integrating the SDK directly. Picks the subject DID, the schema, and the payload; signs and submits.
  • Vellum webpage improvements and own domain. Polish of the existing Vellum dashboard surface (consolidation of identity and reputation views, navigation, copy) and acquisition of a dedicated domain to replace the current vellum-lyart.vercel.app URL.

SDK additions (planned for @ckb-ccc/did-ckb):

import { readClaims, writeClaim } from "@ckb-ccc/did-ckb";

const claims = await readClaims(client, { subject: builderDid });

await writeClaim(signer, {
  subject: builderDid,
  schema: "vellum.task.v1",
  payload: { task_id: 42, rating: 5, link: "..." },
});

Key CKB features used: Cell model (subject-owned claim Cells, capacity-as-storage-rent), Type Script validation, did:ckb identifier algorithm (BLAKE2b type-id pattern), Molecule encoding for Cell data, DAG-CBOR for schema payloads, witness-attached did:plc migration (already shipping in PR #376).

External dependencies: @ckb-ccc/core, @ckb-ccc/did-ckb (the SDK we are extending), @ipld/dag-cbor, @noble/curves (already in use), OAuth providers for the social platforms above.

Open source commitment: all Type Scripts, SDK additions, scoring engine, and frontend code published under MIT license.

6.3 Design Rationale

On-chain claim Cells, not a Vellum database. Portability is the point. If Vellum disappears, the data lives, and any other reader can build a new viewer or scorer. Other CKB apps integrate without coordinating with Vellum, by reading claims directly via the SDK.

Subject-owned Cells. Self-sovereign reputation. The holder controls every record about them and can destroy any record they no longer wish to retain. Privacy through consent to retain, not consent to view. The Cell model makes this natural; EVM-based attestation systems cannot do this cleanly without off-chain workarounds.

Schemas as conventions, not contract-enforced types. New schemas (ckboost.task.v1, ckboost.hackathon.v1, ckbpop.attendance.v1, future ones) do not require a Type Script upgrade. Issuers iterate at the speed of their products. The same convention powers CKBoost integrating tomorrow without forking the spec.

Issuer-pays storage rent. Issuers commit capacity for the claims they make, which acts as a natural Sybil deterrent (spam claims cost the issuer real CKB) and aligns with CKB’s design philosophy. Subjects recover capacity when they destroy a Cell.

Tradeoffs considered. A simpler design would have Vellum hold all the reputation data in its own database and expose it via API. That is faster to ship but creates the same lock-in problem that the community has flagged with CKBoost. Putting the data on chain costs slightly more in implementation effort but is the only way the “portable” claim is actually true.

Security: Type Scripts are small and single-purpose. Initial testing combines internal vetting with public review during the testnet phase. A formal audit is out of scope for this proposal.

Alignment with CKB’s long-term philosophy: storage rent (issuers pay for their claims), permissionless innovation (anyone issues, anyone reads), self-sovereignty (holder owns everything about themselves on chain).

6.4 Fee model and sustainability

The product does not charge fees. Sustainability comes from three sources:

  1. No per-protocol fee, no token. The reputation primitive is open infrastructure. Users pay the standard CKB cell creation cost for their DID (refundable on deactivation). Vellum does not capture value from claim issuance or reading.
  2. Issuer-pays storage rent for claims. Vellum is not on the hook for claim Cell capacity. Issuers (CKBoost, CKB-PoP, future grant DAOs, individual reviewers, others) pay for the claims they make.
  3. Optional premium tiers in future. Custom profile-page domains, advanced analytics for issuers, branded issuer surfaces. None of these are required, and none are proposed in this grant. The core remains free.

There is no protocol fee, no token, and no capture of value from claim issuance or reading.

Key Benefits for CKB

  • Sybil-resistant governance for emerging CKB community programs. The reputation primitive gives upcoming governance designs (gated sub-communities, POAP-style eligibility, crowdfunding, grant programs) a portable, queryable signal of genuine ecosystem participation, mitigating wallet-splitting and token-acquisition attacks that pure token-weighted governance is structurally vulnerable to.
  • An open reputation primitive any CKB app can use. Governance programs read it for eligibility gates and participation weighting. Grant programs read it for Sybil resistance. Wallets render verified socials from it. Platforms write to it to attach signed claims to a builder’s record.
  • Portable identity and reputation that survives any single app. A builder’s record is theirs, not a platform’s. If CKBoost (or any future platform) goes offline, the builder’s track record persists on chain.
  • Concrete day-one integration with CKBoost. This grant ships a working testnet integration where CKBoost gains a richer identity layer via did:ckb and quest-completion claims feed reputation scoring. The pattern generalises: CKB-PoP can sign attendance for events, future grant DAOs can sign grant-completion claims, all without coordination with Vellum beyond the published schemas.
  • Matures the did:ckb stack through real integration testing. The basic DID operations are shipping; what they need next is exposure to real consumer integration so the rough edges surface. CKBoost integration plus the governance gating reference give the stack two distinct integration patterns to test against on testnet.
  • Developer tooling. Two new SDK functions (readClaims, writeClaim) land in @ckb-ccc/did-ckb. Any CKB app integrates in roughly 20 lines of code.

Detailed Deliverables & Milestones

Initial Funding

  • ETA: Week 0
  • Budget: $1,750 USD (25%)
  • Deliverables:
    • Proposal accepted.
    • Public roadmap and GitHub project board live.

Milestone 1: Claim Cell + SDK + Scoring engine

  • ETA: Q4 2026 (weeks 1-4)
  • Budget: $1,750 USD (25%)
  • Deliverables:
    • Claim Cell Type Script deployed on CKB testnet at a published address.
    • readClaims and writeClaim PR’d into @ckb-ccc/did-ckb.
    • Scoring engine issues verified-social claims (GitHub, Discord, Telegram, Bluesky) via OAuth.
    • Schema specs documented and published.

Milestone 2: Builder profile pages + CKBoost integration + webpage polish

  • ETA: Q4 2026 (weeks 5-8)
  • Budget: $1,750 USD (25%)
  • Deliverables:
    • Public builder profile page at /profile/<did> showing identity, verified socials, ecosystem activity, and a reputation score with per-category breakdown (technical, community, contribution, tenure, recency) derived from the claim history.
    • CKBoost integration on testnet: CKBoost-signed quest-completion claims feed the scoring engine and surface in both the score breakdown and the activity feed.
    • Vellum webpage improvements (consolidated identity and reputation views, navigation, copy).

Milestone 3: Governance gating reference + mini demo + issuance UI + own domain

  • ETA: Q4 2026 (weeks 9-12)
  • Budget: $1,750 USD (25%)
  • Deliverables:
    • Governance gating reference: a small example contract (or off-chain checker, depending on the consuming program’s design) that reads readClaims to determine eligibility, plus documented integration patterns aimed at upcoming CKBuilders programs (gated sub-communities, POAP-style eligibility, crowdfunding).
    • Mini interactive demo at /demo/governance that wires the reference into a sample vote (paste a DID, see eligibility plus derived participation weight from the claim history, cast a sample vote against a dummy proposal).
    • Issuance UI for ecosystem partners (form-based claim issuance for CKB-PoP, future grant DAOs, anyone with a credible attestation to make).
    • Acquisition and configuration of a dedicated Vellum domain to replace the current Vercel subdomain.
    • Testnet validation pass across all M1-M3 deliverables.

Acceptance criteria (per milestone): Each milestone closes only when (a) the named on-chain artifact is deployed at a published address on testnet, (b) the corresponding GitHub PR is merged to the Vellum repository, and (c) a designated reviewer posts an approval comment on the proposal thread. Reviewer designations will be confirmed during the discussion phase.

The scope is deliberately concentrated. Cross-chain export, formal audits, and ZK proof-of-personhood integrations are flagged in section 10 as out of scope to keep this proposal focused and credible.

Budget Breakdown

The $7,000 USD equivalent funds 12 weeks of solo developer work focused on shipping a testnet reputation primitive with CKBoost integration, plus polish of the Vellum webpage and acquisition of its own domain. The categories below mirror the CFDAO template structure.

Development costs: $6,000

  • Smart contracts / Type Scripts (Claim Cell Type Script): ~$2,000.
  • SDK additions to @ckb-ccc/did-ckb (readClaims, writeClaim, helpers, tests): ~$1,000.
  • Off-chain scoring engine (OAuth integrations for GitHub, Discord, Telegram, Bluesky; signal pullers, schema writers, tests): ~$1,500.
  • Frontend (Vellum reputation dashboard, builder profile pages, governance gating reference and mini demo, issuance UI for ecosystem partners, Vellum webpage improvements): ~$1,500.

Security audit: $0

  • No formal third-party audit in this proposal. Type Scripts are small and single-purpose; initial deployment uses internal testing plus public community review during the testnet phase.

Infrastructure / hosting: $500

  • OAuth proxy hosting, Vellum dashboard and public profile-page hosting, dedicated domain acquisition and DNS for Vellum’s own URL.
  • On-chain Cell capacity for new claims is paid by issuers per claim and is negligible per update.

Project management: absorbed in development.

  • Solo developer; PM overhead minimal and absorbed into development time.

Documentation & community engagement: $500

  • Schema spec publishing, integration guides, forum engagement during the build period.

Total: $7,000

Out-of-budget items (full list in section 10): formal security audit, paid marketing or BD outreach, long-term maintenance beyond 6 months post-M3, and specialized infrastructure beyond standard hosting. If the Nervos Community Catalyst offers to cover webhosting, domain, or IPFS storage as it did for CKBoost, that is welcomed but not assumed in this ask.

Out-of-Scope / Future Funding Needs

The following are deliberately out of scope for this grant:

  • Formal security audit and mainnet promotion of the new Type Scripts. The reputation primitive (Claim Cell Type Script) ships on testnet only in this proposal.
  • Long-term maintenance beyond 6 months post-disbursement of M3 (see section 11 for the maintenance commitment in this grant).
  • Vellum DID as a sign-in identity provider for CKBoost (full Level-3 integration). This proposal commits to integration where CKBoost signs quest-completion claims and Vellum profile pages render CKBoost activity. Full sign-in replacement, where users authenticate to CKBoost with did:ckb instead of CKBoost’s native identity, is out of scope.
  • Cross-chain reputation export to Ethereum, Polygon, or other chains. The claim format is open, so this remains technically possible, but it is out of scope for this proposal.
  • ZK proof-of-personhood integration (wrapping Human Passport, World ID, or building a CKB-native equivalent).
  • Paid marketing or BD outreach. Other CKB platforms can integrate via documented schema conventions; no paid outreach is budgeted.

Risk & Mitigation

  • Technical complexity of the Claim Cell Type Script. The Type Script is small, single-purpose, and follows patterns already shipping in @ckb-ccc/did-ckb. The main implementation risks are getting the CKBoost integration reliable end-to-end and getting the off-chain scoring engine stable across multiple OAuth providers; mitigated by close design review at the milestone boundaries.
  • Adoption risk: will governance programs and other CKB apps integrate? The governance gating reference implementation ships with the grant and demonstrates the consumer pattern end-to-end. CKBoost and CKB-PoP are flagged issuer paths whose stated open questions the extension addresses. Adoption beyond the deliverables in this proposal is upside, not a requirement for delivery.
  • Solo developer execution risk. Track record exists: Vellum v1 already shipped on mainnet and testnet, and PR #376 was reviewed and merged by a CCC maintainer. The 12-week scope is conservative given an existing codebase as foundation.
  • Sybil farming of social claims. OAuth-verified social signals require real platform accounts; combining signals across multiple platforms raises the cost of farming. Reputation is informational input to human reviewers, not financially load-bearing, so adversarial pressure is bounded. Hardening (proof-of-personhood, decay weights) is out of scope for this proposal.
  • CKB price volatility affecting the budget. Grant amount is requested as a USD equivalent. The CKB amount for each disbursement is calculated at pay time using the then-current price, so CKB price movement between proposal posting and any milestone disbursement does not affect the USD value the project receives.
  • Community adoption depends on reviewer engagement. Reviewer designations will be confirmed during the discussion phase before voting begins. Public reviewer acknowledgement has held in prior approved proposals.

Maintenance commitment in this grant: Vellum’s existing identity dashboard on mainnet continues to be maintained as it has been. The reputation extension built in this grant will be maintained on testnet for at least 6 months following M3 disbursement, with best-effort upkeep beyond that period. SDK additions to @ckb-ccc/did-ckb will be kept current with major upstream @ckb-ccc/core releases on a best-effort basis.

Closing / Call to Action

Vellum’s identity layer is shipping on mainnet. This proposal funds the next chapter on testnet: making did:ckb genuinely useful by attaching portable, self-sovereign reputation to it, with CKBoost as the day-one plugin integration partner, governance as the load-bearing reference consumer, and an open standard any other CKB app can plug into as either an issuer or a reader.

We appreciate your consideration. Feedback, questions, and integration interest from other CKB platforms are welcome in the discussion below.

posts.cooked:
Based on the Metaforo tally at close, the outcome is PASSED. Approval is 64.37% with total voting weight 242,742,014 CKB.

Post-close verification has been completed using CKB DAO Watchdog, together with a manual sanity check. The verification cross-checks Metaforo-recorded voting weights against on-chain Nervos DAO deposit weights. In this run, all entries match.

The Vellum V2 proposal is confirmed as PASSED.

Vellum Milestone 1 delivery report

Implementation for Vellum’s first grant milestone is complete and ready for community review.

M1 established the foundation for portable reputation on did:ckb: the Claim Cell contracts are deployed on CKB Testnet, @usevellum/sdk is published with Claim Cell read and write APIs, all four planned account-verification flows can issue claims through Vellum’s Testnet issuer, the schema registry is published, and the dashboard computes a transparent score from the resulting on-chain evidence.

  • Repository: GitHub - truthixify/vellum: Portable identity and verifiable reputation for builders on Nervos CKB. · GitHub
  • Live website: https://usevellum.xyz
  • Live dashboard: https://dashboard.usevellum.xyz
  • Approved proposal and report thread: [DIS] Vellum: Reputation Extension on did:ckb
  • Public roadmap: Vellum Reputation Extension · GitHub
  • M1 issue and pull request record: GitHub · Where software is built

Delivery against the proposal

Approved M1 deliverable Result
Claim Cell Type Script deployed on CKB Testnet at a published address Complete. Claim Type and the separate reusable DID Lock are live as independent Type ID code cells.
readClaims and writeClaim SDK additions Complete and published in the Vellum-owned @usevellum/sdk package. The ownership change from the original upstream-package plan is explained below.
Verified-social claim issuance for GitHub, Discord, Telegram, and Bluesky Complete. Each flow verifies account control, binds issuance to a wallet-proven subject DID, and submits Claim Cells through the configured Vellum issuer.
Schema specifications documented and published Complete. Seven immutable v1 schema manifests, hashes, parsers, examples, and specifications are published.

The GitHub milestone now has no open implementation items. It records 16 completed issues and 16 merged milestone pull requests covering the protocol, contracts, deployment, SDK, verification service, scoring policy, schemas, and dashboard. Final npm publication followed through pull requests #50 and #51.

What shipped

Claim Cell protocol and Testnet contracts

Vellum now has a small on-chain assertion format built around two CKB scripts:

  • Claim Type validates canonical Claim data, fresh authorization from the current controller of the issuer’s did:ckb, timestamps, unique claim IDs, schema binding, and the subject lock.
  • DID Lock lets a Claim Cell remain attached to a stable did:ckb identity while following controller rotation. Claim Type can also accept another complete CKB lock when an integration chooses that subject model.

The final protocol does not use a detached issuer signature. The issuer’s current controller lock authorizes the complete CKB transaction, and the subject controls the output Cell. A holder can consume a claim they no longer want to retain and recover its capacity.

Both contracts are deployed in one CKB Testnet transaction while retaining independent Type ID identities and upgrade paths:

  • Deployment transaction: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0xaf693346282063a5d51f79d180fc807cdba1b8ac9d7af30085ff0aa190e2686c
  • Claim Type: output 0x0, code hash 0xfb2757e524b3f83161d8b85b8b3e00186e2019ff04f5dfe833c5a72731e13157
  • DID Lock: output 0x1, code hash 0xe1562cc57b4bd91619ada2f7e74d63805ea7038a7b6de0b18a529d51aa883d2d
  • Machine-readable deployment record: vellum/deployments/testnet.json at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • Protocol specification: vellum/docs/claim-cell.md at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub

Fresh release builds are compared byte for byte with the live Testnet code cells. The current Claim Type binary is 47,752 bytes and the DID Lock is 30,336 bytes. Measured Claim Type paths range from 14,964 cycles for destruction to 146,842 cycles for creation with issuer replacement.

Claim SDK

The Vellum SDK now provides typed Claim Cell codecs and the two main integration paths:

  • readClaims scans every indexer page for an exact subject lock, supports issuer and schema filters, decodes Molecule and canonical DAG-CBOR, evaluates expiry at an explicit application checkpoint, and reports malformed or unverifiable evidence without silently accepting it.
  • writeClaim and writeClaims build prepared, balanced, unsigned transactions with dynamic capacity calculation, fresh issuer-controller authorization, explicit payer behavior, and stable output metadata. Signing and broadcasting remain explicit caller actions.

The live Testnet suite covers same-issuer and cross-issuer reads, single and atomic batch construction, and holder-controlled claim destruction with capacity recovery. Public fixtures include:

  • Known live claim: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x9e32511bcaa49d89421d070d28eded7168fa9010a007659151e7f8928caff91c
  • Cross-issuer claim: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0xdd3ba6f4574568df0f82a1a9201598da697ff4ce28b3b1cc7a28289ef2319cb3
  • Claim creation and later capacity recovery: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x6003e4e13d757a02003cc23d156f100ff351ca28f0d67df7f04bf71d18255640 and https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x647a5253321acb45e8aa07195f0414678831f955610bdfcce59efa1107638816
  • SDK guide: vellum/docs/claim-sdk.md at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • Package guide: vellum/packages/sdk/README.md at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@usevellum/sdk
  • GitHub release: Release @usevellum/sdk@0.1.0 · truthixify/vellum · GitHub

Version 0.1.0 is available from npm. A Changesets-based GitHub workflow validates and packs release candidates, publishes approved releases, and creates the matching Git tag and GitHub release.

Verification, issuance, and reputation

The dashboard runs a server-side verification and issuance service on Vercel. The connected wallet proves control of the selected subject DID; Vellum’s published Testnet issuer authorizes, funds, and submits the Claim Cell transaction. OAuth credentials, OIDC tokens, and app passwords are transient and are not stored as reputation data.

The four planned account sources are live:

  • GitHub: verifies the stable account and can issue separate evidence for qualifying public work in reviewed CKB ecosystem repositories.
  • Discord: verifies the stable account and can issue separate membership evidence for configured CKB communities and roles.
  • Telegram: verifies the stable account through Telegram OIDC and can issue current membership evidence for configured Nervos groups where the Vellum bot is an administrator.
  • Bluesky: authenticates with a scoped app password, resolves the stable AT Protocol DID, closes the temporary session, and issues the identity claim.

The issuer identity and transaction policy are public at https://dashboard.usevellum.xyz/api/issuer. The current issuer is did:ckb:hlvxrdt3e7iwvuxdmbvejp6hc4yoo3no on CKB Testnet.

The read-only scoring service applies the frozen vellum.reputation.v5 policy on demand. It returns an integer score out of 1,000 across Technical, Contribution, Community, Tenure, and Recency, together with the exact Claim Cells and policy rules behind every point. Duplicate, superseded, expired, untrusted, or malformed evidence cannot contribute silently, and incomplete chain state returns unavailable rather than a partial score. There is no private reputation database and no opaque score claim.

  • Verification service documentation: vellum/docs/verification-service.md at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • Scoring policy and API: vellum/docs/reputation-scoring.md at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • Live verification UI: Vellum Dashboard - Identity and reputation on CKB
  • Live reputation UI: Vellum Dashboard - Identity and reputation on CKB

Published schemas and dashboard

Seven current verifier outputs have immutable v1 specifications, canonical JSON manifests, pinned CKB hashes, typed parsers, and validated examples:

  • vellum.social.github.v1
  • vellum.contribution.github.v1
  • vellum.social.discord.v1
  • vellum.community.discord.v1
  • vellum.social.telegram.v1
  • vellum.community.telegram.v1
  • vellum.social.bluesky.v1

Registry: vellum/docs/schemas at main · truthixify/vellum · GitHub

The dashboard now exposes the selected identity’s aggregate score throughout the live experience, provides a public evidence breakdown and share card, shows every Claim Cell returned by verification, and keeps later issuance and governance work out of the live M1 navigation. The public site and dashboard also share one app identity and follow the system theme until the user chooses an explicit override.

Implementation evidence

Workstream Merged pull requests
Protocol, contracts, and deployment #31 protocol, #32 contracts, #33 Testnet deployment
SDK #34 API design, #35 reader, #36 writer, #37 package preparation, #50 release automation, #51 v0.1.0 release
Verification and scoring #38 service, #40 GitHub identity, #41 scoring, #43 Discord, #44 GitHub contributions, #45 Telegram, #46 Bluesky
Schemas and product review #47 schema registry, #49 dashboard consistency

The Claim Cell protocol and SDK boundary both received independent public review before M1 delivery was finalized. Review findings changed the design materially, including separating Claim Type from DID Lock, accepting arbitrary CKB subject locks, removing reusable detached claim signatures, tightening issuer-history handling, and clarifying package ownership. The protocol review is recorded in Vellum PR #31, and the package-boundary review is recorded in CCC PR #562.

Verification results

The final M1 pull request CI run is public at Release @usevellum/sdk · truthixify/vellum@451a36a · GitHub and passed both jobs.

  • 326 Bun/TypeScript tests passed across 53 files with 0 failures and 1,105 assertions.
  • Formatting, ESLint, strict TypeScript checks, both Vite production builds, executable SDK examples, and package inspection passed.
  • 21 Rust parser and CKB-VM integration tests passed for Claim Type and DID Lock.
  • Six public CKB Testnet SDK checks passed against committed on-chain fixtures.
  • The deployment verifier rebuilt both contracts and matched every byte, hash, capacity, Type ID, and locator against the live code cells.
  • The final dashboard audit passed 138 responsive route checks across 390 px, 768 px, and 1440 px in both themes. A separate 10-case browser pass verified system-theme changes and manual overrides in both applications.
  • The release workflow at Merge pull request #51 from truthixify/changeset-release/main · truthixify/vellum@e60bee3 · GitHub validated, packed, and published @usevellum/sdk@0.1.0, then created the matching GitHub release.

Changes from the original implementation plan

One ownership boundary changed after review. The proposal placed readClaims and writeClaim in @ckb-ccc/did-ckb. CCC PR #562 presented that implementation for upstream review, and the maintainer recommended a standalone Vellum SDK because the Claim protocol is application-specific and not used elsewhere in CCC. The PR was closed after that recommendation was accepted. The final design keeps DID identifier and identity primitives in @ckb-ccc/did-ckb, while Claim Cell codecs, readers, transaction builders, release ownership, and Vellum policy live in the Vellum-owned @usevellum/sdk package. This preserves the small integration surface promised in the proposal without coupling the general DID package to Vellum’s protocol. @usevellum/sdk@0.1.0 is now published on npm; generic CCC utilities can still be contributed upstream separately when a concrete reusable need is identified.

The proposal also used “OAuth” as shorthand for every social connection. The implementation uses the appropriate provider mechanism instead: OAuth for GitHub and Discord, OIDC for Telegram, and a scoped app password plus stable-DID resolution for Bluesky.

Finally, issuance and scoring are deliberately separate. The verification service issues factual Claim Cells; the scoring service reads those Cells and applies a versioned policy on demand. This keeps the evidence portable and lets another application apply a different policy without depending on a Vellum-owned score record.

Testing, feedback, and review

M1 is live on CKB Testnet, and community testing would be useful before the milestone is confirmed:

  • Inspect the public score and evidence for did:ckb:4kiidiczwthgxj7dltzkzopgbwu3v6jc at Vellum Dashboard - Identity and reputation on CKB.
  • Connect a CKB Testnet wallet at Vellum Dashboard - Identity and reputation on CKB and test one of the GitHub, Discord, Telegram, or Bluesky verification flows against a DID the wallet controls.
  • Install @usevellum/sdk and try the documented Claim Cell read or transaction-building APIs.

Please share test results, unexpected behavior, integration questions, or other feedback in this thread or through Issues · truthixify/vellum · GitHub. I am also requesting review of the delivery evidence above and the designated reviewer sign-off required to confirm M1.

Next milestone

M2 moves from the foundation to the public builder record: richer public profile pages, reusable schema renderers, the CKBoost integration and claim format, and continued website and documentation work. The Claim Cell, SDK, verification, and scoring foundation delivered here is what those surfaces will read and extend.

Thank you to everyone who reviewed the protocol and SDK, tested the verification flows, and raised issues during implementation. Questions and independent checks of the linked evidence are welcome.

Vellum Milestone 2 delivery report

Implementation for Vellum’s second grant milestone is complete and ready for community review.

M2 turns the Claim Cell foundation delivered in M1 into a public builder record and a real partner integration. Vellum now provides shareable profiles for did:ckb identities, renders issuer-backed evidence, and applies a transparent reputation policy. CKBoost can issue portable quest-completion claims through its production Testnet flow, with one completion validated end to end from the reward transaction to the public profile and score.

  • Repository: GitHub - truthixify/vellum: Portable identity and verifiable reputation for builders on Nervos CKB. · GitHub
  • Live website: https://usevellum.xyz
  • Live dashboard: https://dashboard.usevellum.xyz
  • Public profile with a real CKBoost claim: Public did:ckb profile | Vellum
  • Vellum documentation: Vellum | Portable identity and reputation on CKB
  • Approved proposal and report thread: [DIS] Vellum: Reputation Extension on did:ckb
  • Public roadmap: Vellum Reputation Extension · GitHub
  • M2 issue and pull request record: M2: Builder profiles + CKBoost integration + webpage Milestone · truthixify/vellum · GitHub
  • CKBoost integration pull request: feat: add Vellum quest Claim Cell issuance by truthixify · Pull Request #65 · Alive24/CKBoost · GitHub
  • Vellum Test Campaign: CKBoost

Delivery against the proposal

Approved M2 deliverable Result
Public builder profile at /profile/<did> showing identity, verified socials, ecosystem activity, and a per-category reputation score Complete. Public profiles resolve the live DID document, read the complete Claim Cell record, and show profile details, verified accounts, category scores, evidence, and source transactions without requiring a wallet connection.
CKBoost integration on Testnet, with CKBoost-signed quest completions feeding reputation scoring and public activity Complete. CKBoost issues ckboost.quest.v1 Claim Cells after confirmed reward or points claims through its own issuer DID and funded server-side signer. A real completion is publicly readable, rendered on the subject’s profile, and scored exactly once.
Vellum webpage improvements covering identity and reputation views, navigation, and copy Complete. The public landing page now presents the working product and confirmed Testnet evidence, with live paths for builders, issuers, integrators, and community reviewers. Task-oriented documentation covers the same shipped flows.

The GitHub milestone has no open implementation items. It records 10 closed issues and six merged milestone pull requests, together with the linked dashboard follow-up in PR #55 and the upstream CKBoost implementation in Alive24/CKBoost PR #65.

What shipped

Public builder profiles and Claim Cell renderers

Every live Testnet did:ckb can now be opened through a directly linkable public profile. The profile combines the live DID document, optional services.profile data, verified accounts, the current reputation result, accepted and excluded evidence, and the source transaction for each Claim Cell. Direct profile loads work without a connected wallet and expose profile-specific canonical and social metadata.

Known Claim Cell schemas render through an exact-hash registry. Each registered renderer validates its payload before presentation, while malformed or unknown claims remain inspectable through a bounded raw-data view instead of being silently discarded. The shared registry covers every published Vellum schema, including ckboost.quest.v1.

Implementation: PR #52 and PR #53.

CKBoost issuance, rendering, and scoring

CKBoost now reconstructs the campaign, quest, user, approval, and reward provenance after a confirmed reward or points claim. It verifies that the selected active DID controller authorized the reward transaction and matches the approved CKBoost user, then issues through a CKBoost-controlled Testnet issuer. Signed transaction state and issuer coordination are persisted with strong consistency so retries reuse the exact transaction and cannot create a duplicate completion claim.

The canonical ckboost.quest.v1 schema preserves the campaign Type ID, quest ID, CKBoost user Type ID, completion timestamp, raw points, approval transaction, and final reward-claim transaction. The public renderer exposes those fields and transaction links. Raw CKBoost points remain informational; the versioned Vellum policy scores eligible completion depth and campaign breadth independently rather than treating platform points as reputation points.

The active vellum.reputation.v7 policy accepts claims only from the configured CKBoost issuer and a versioned eligible-quest registry. Untrusted issuers, unregistered quests, duplicates, malformed payloads, and ineligible completions do not contribute silently.

Implementation: Vellum PR #56, CKBoost PR #65, and Vellum end-to-end validation PR #59.

Public website and documentation

The illustrative homepage has been replaced by a public product experience centered on portable identity, issuer-backed evidence, and transparent reputation. It exposes the confirmed CKBoost Testnet claim as inspectable product evidence and provides working entry points for identity management, public profiles, schemas, SDK integration, grant progress, and the published reputation policy.

The documentation now has separate task-oriented paths for builders, claim issuers, application integrators, and did:ckb identity resolution. Pages have persistent reference navigation, anchored section navigation, executable SDK examples, and accessible copy success and recovery states. Legacy identity-documentation fragments continue to resolve to the restored identity guide.

Implementation: PR #60 and PR #61.

Follow-on ecosystem integrations

CKBoost is the first completed external issuer integration, and other builders in the CKB ecosystem have already reached out about integrating Vellum into their projects:

  • @Ajay for Klaveroq: a trusted work marketplace for talent discovery, milestone delivery, and protected payments.
  • @Ayoub_Lesfer for CrowdCell: an on-chain crowdfunding platform built on CKB.
  • Hamza’s Legacy for Kweela: a platform for people, creators, communities, and brands.
  • @anihdev for CKB Governance: governance and SubDAO work on CKB.

These are follow-on integrations rather than completed M2 deliverables. I will continue working with each builder to define and implement an integration that fits the project’s actual trust and product requirements. Other ecosystem teams that want to issue portable evidence or consume Vellum reputation are welcome to reply in this thread or reach out through GitHub Issues to discuss an integration path.

Real Testnet evidence

  • Subject DID: did:ckb:omdrzidnxy3lrdrwc6bo4sll6zljhuar
  • CKBoost issuer DID: did:ckb:tlitdhrdn7wdzmktk3kzhfua3ivpgiq2
  • Schema: ckboost.quest.v1, hash 0x6f0fe424320c73627ac544d6666841623c2b15b88ffc93818dc9f78752dd8fae
  • Campaign: Vellum Test Campaign, Type ID 0x3aee953b010d5861b521017839e9f137047756b81bbc1ac78d13d5c6e9f5c9ad
  • Quest: Send the Vellum Dashboard Link, quest ID 1
  • Claim ID: 0x015f760b79be6f81444e7338a306db9b0dcb814052740e3fc33eaf79c06d226e
  • Claim Cell: transaction 0x83f547f606bce2d6163e997eff45463f09956725e9217c88c1e97a52e7c3e1f2, output 0: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x83f547f606bce2d6163e997eff45463f09956725e9217c88c1e97a52e7c3e1f2
  • CKBoost approval transaction: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x2cf616b312036b6daeec1426123900be80eb1b5293ca57fcff58dad632ef9331
  • CKBoost reward-claim transaction: https://testnet.explorer.nervos.org/transaction/0x3349c6bae7a6776036840bf5cb0cf026287ac0af8872e343dd3327b1d4704110
  • Occupied capacity: 738 CKB; issuance fee: 0.00044219 CKB
  • Reputation result: the eligible completion contributes 20 Contribution points exactly once under vellum.reputation.v7: Vellum Dashboard - Identity and reputation on CKB

Implementation evidence

Workstream Merged pull requests
Public profiles and rendering #52 public profiles, #53 schema renderers, #55 additional DID action
CKBoost integration #56 schema, renderer, and scoring, Alive24/CKBoost #65 issuer integration, #59 live Testnet validation
Website and documentation #60 public landing page, #61 documentation sections

Verification results

The final M2 merge CI run is public at Merge pull request #61 from truthixify/feat/documentation-sections · truthixify/vellum@8d01a77 · GitHub and passed both the Quality and Claim Cell contract jobs.

  • 401 Bun/TypeScript tests passed across 69 files with 0 failures and 1,537 assertions.
  • Formatting, ESLint, strict TypeScript checks, both Vite production builds, executable SDK examples, SDK package inspection, Rust formatting, Rust checks, lints, CKB-VM tests, and contract release-size reporting passed.
  • The reproducible live CKBoost profile test passed 28 assertions against the confirmed Testnet Claim Cell; the reputation Testnet suite passed nine assertions covering issuer resolution and scoring.
  • The CKBoost integration reported 19 Jest suites with 78 passing tests, a successful production build covering 22 routes and 11 Pagefind pages, a successful Netlify Functions build, and a read-only check of its active funded issuer DID.
  • Landing-page Lighthouse results were 96 mobile performance, 100 mobile accessibility, and 100 mobile SEO under the default simulated Slow 4G profile; desktop performance, accessibility, and SEO were all 100, with a 0.5-second LCP.
  • Browser checks covered the public profile, landing page, and documentation at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths. The production landing page, documentation routes, public CKBoost-backed profile, and reputation URL all returned HTTP 200 during final report validation.

Testing, feedback, and review

M2 is live on CKB Testnet, and community testing would be useful before the milestone is confirmed:

  • Inspect the real CKBoost evidence and score at Public did:ckb profile | Vellum.
  • Compare the public profile with the Claim Cell, approval transaction, reward transaction, and vellum.reputation.v7 result linked above.
  • Review the builder, issuer, integrator, and identity guides at Vellum | Portable identity and reputation on CKB and try the documented SDK flows.
  • Report unexpected behavior or integration questions through Issues · truthixify/vellum · GitHub.

Please share test results, unexpected behavior, integration questions, or other feedback in this thread. I am also requesting review of the delivery evidence above and the designated reviewer sign-off required to confirm M2.

Next milestone

M3 will demonstrate the consumer side of the reputation primitive through a governance-gating reference, a live gated-poll demo, and a general partner issuance UI. It will also complete the planned domain and redirect work, funding transparency, and the final cross-milestone Testnet validation pass.

Thank you to @Alive24 for working through the CKBoost integration design, merging the upstream implementation, configuring the Testnet issuer, and helping validate the production flow. Thank you as well to everyone who tested the campaign, claim issuance, profile, and scoring path. Questions and independent checks of the linked evidence are welcome.
